title: Critical-Bias Average Complexity of OR
statement: For each positive integer $n$, let $p_n=1-\exp(-\log(2)/n)$ and consider the OR function on $n$ signs, equal to $+1$ when every input is $+1$ and $-1$ otherwise. Under the product distribution in which each input is independently $-1$ with probability $p_n$, take the infimum of the expected number of coordinate queries over all finite randomized decision trees that compute this OR function with zero error. This infimum, divided by $n$, tends to $1/(2\log 2)$ as $n\to\infty$.
hypotheses_covered: $n$ ranges over nonnegative integers tending to infinity
The coordinate inputs are independent, with probability $p_n=1-\exp(-\log(2)/n)$ of being $-1$
The computed function is OR, returning $+1$ exactly when all inputs are $+1$
The complexity is the infimum expected query count over finite randomized decision trees computing the function exactly
